metadata.prompt:
I want to think of something big for deciduous: 

A methodology to have a skill/command/whatever that will be used for you to do archaeology in a repo that _didnt_ have deciduous already set up

I've done this twice now and have some examples of DAGs I've made you make and they include prompts etc

with that do you think we could build an archaelogy tool?

---

and also use the entire commit history, commit by commit, assuming the project has been good with git hygeine 

for structuring the graph, for each logical premise that comes as a series of pieces of work through issues, commits, PRs, etc, we want to build those up as if we were making a "branch" for each one, each of the branches is linked to the root beginning node but they spread out in parallel. Sometimes a new branch might logically be the child of another. that should be marked too. it needs to be VERY deep for all fronts that it works from.

title: Build archaeology skill for bootstrapping deciduous in existing projects
